newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico first half March inflation.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico first half March inflation.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index for the first two weeks of March came in at 0.66 percent, Banco de Mexico said.
The following are reactions from economists.
American Express Financial Services director of economic analysis for emerging markets, James Carlen, said: "This reaffirms the story that is unfolding that inflation is under control in Mexico.
"It came in pretty much as expected. The number supports the general consensus that the higher inflation earlier in the year was transitory."
A Reuters' survey of economists found expectations of a 0.71 percent rise for the first half of the month.
"It was a bit below what we were expecting. There were seasonal factors as well as the downward weight of a strong exchange rate," said I.D.E.A. economist Gene Frieda.
He said there will be a signficant lag from the recent weakening of the peso on inflation.
"If anything it (the inflation number) will help interest rates and may be used as an excuse to bring down rates faster," he said.
MMS International said it believes the market will react calmly to the lower-than-expected inflation "as it confirms the previous forecasts for all 1997."
The consumer price index rose 2.57 percent in January and 1.68 percent in February.
